watchers.reasoning: Pressure is declining (-7.3 kPa/h) but hasn't sustained past -5 kPa/h for 3 hours yet.
Residual is 0.000, inside the healthy band (0σ from baseline mean — see the unresolved-baseline note).
Temperature moved 0.273°C in the same hour as the degradation (lag ≈ 0) — this is NOT an early warning signal, it moves with the event.
Some gap-filled records in this window, but nothing clustering or uncalibrated.

listener_validation.note: The young dragons' ears are exactly as accurate as the sensors — never earlier, never later.

diagnosis.headline: Water pressure slipping, not critical yet
diagnosis.recommended_action: Keep an eye on the water pressure trend and recheck in a few hours rather than waking anyone now.
diagnosis.reasoning: Cloudy's note says 'the pipes complain first' — pressure dropping faster than -5 kPa/h for 3 straight hours means trouble, and right now it's at -7.3 kPa/h but hasn't held that long. It's not confirmed to be the start of the same pattern that caused the two past total water failures, so no need to panic yet. Separately, note that Entry 4's claim about cold air giving early warning is disputed — the data shows temperature and airflow drop together, not one before the other, so don't rely on feeling cold as a warning.
diagnosis.caveat: Only two past water episodes exist in history, so this pattern-match is based on very few examples and the sensors cannot forecast a brand-new fault starting.

ledger_snapshot.claim: Note 1 — 'the pipes complain first'. A pressure slope steeper than -5 kPa/h sustained for 3 hours precedes total water failure.
ledger_snapshot.source: Person A, Figure 6: pressure_slope_6h separates escalating from resolving episodes by ~hour 4 of warning. Both recorded water episodes escalated.

ledger_snapshot.claim: Note 2 — 'the library has a rhythm'. The young dragons' ears track system_status as accurately as the sensors do.
ledger_snapshot.source: Person A, Figure 4: sound_event maps 1:1 onto system_status with zero off-diagonal. True, but it carries no information the sensors lack — which is why it is shown in its own panel and never enters the severity calculation.

ledger_snapshot.claim: Note 3 — 'fans running in circles'. The fans can turn at full power while moving no air.
ledger_snapshot.source: Person A, Figure 3: airflow = 0.1250 x power - 1.5000, r2 = 0.999999. A residual below -0.5006 means the fans are spinning without moving air.

ledger_snapshot.claim: Note 4 — 'cold arrives later'. Temperature is supposed to drop some hours after airflow does, giving early warning.
ledger_snapshot.source: Person A: temperature and airflow drop in the SAME hour, not lagged. Cloudy's note is wrong on this one — there is no head start to be had from watching the cold.

ledger_snapshot.claim: Note 5 — 'missing pieces'. Gaps in the sensor record cluster around incidents.
ledger_snapshot.source: Person A, Figure 7: the 6 gaps scatter across the month with no clustering near incidents. Not enough evidence either way — treated as no rule rather than a refutation.

ledger_snapshot.claim: Onset is not forecastable. A brand-new fault starting cannot be predicted from the sensors.
ledger_snapshot.source: Person A, Figure 5: the t+6h classifier reaches 88.5% accuracy but catches 0 of 24 true onset-precursor rows — the accuracy is pure persistence.
